newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOREST INDUSTRY DENTS FINNISH 1996 EXPORT GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: FOREST INDUSTRY DENTS FINNISH 1996 EXPORT GROWTH.

text.p: Weak forest industry exports slowed export growth to six percent last year from 14 percent in 1995, the National Customs Board (NCB) said on Tuesday.
"The slowdown in exports (growth) was mainly due to the rather weak performance of the forest industry," NCB director Eero Kuisma told a news conference.
The value of last year's paper exports fell 10 percent on 1995 to 45 billion markka in 1996, NCB said in its monthly foreign trade review with the full-year data.
The value of pulp exports fell almost 25 percent year-on-year, but board and speciality paper products showed modest growth, the NCB said.

Wood industry exports fell six percent and sawn goods exports dropped 13 percent year-on-year. Exports of wooden houses increased sharply but the value of furniture exports fell slightly, the NCB said.
The metal industry which comprises the fast-growing electrotechnical sector remained the biggest exporting sector in 1996 with a clear lead ahead of forestry.
Metal industry exports rose over 10 percent to almost 93 billion markka in 1996, lifting the the metal industry's share of total exports by three percentage points to 50 percent, Kuisma said.
Ferry deliveries abroad showed clear growth in 1996, up over 30 percent to 7.5 billion markka. Chemical industry exports also rose sharply, up 16 percent.

The value of imports rose 10 percent year-on-year in 1996 with the strongest 15.6 percent growth in imports of investment goods. The 1996 trade surplus was 44.8 billion markka, down from 47.5 billion in 1995, the NCB said.

The December trade surplus fell to 1.86 billion from the revised 6.37 billion in November. The value of exports fell five percent year-on-year in December while the value of imports rose 15 percent, the NCB said.

The NCB repeated its earlier statement that it will start to publish preliminary foreign trade data seven weeks after the end of each month and detailed foreign trade figures about 10 weeks after the end of each month.
